# Babysitter instructions

For anyone staying with Max (7) and Lily (3). Fridge copy; keep it updated.

## Phone numbers

Mom's cell and Dad's cell are on the fridge door. Poison control: 1-800-222-1222. Dr. Okafor's office (pediatrics) is 555-0142 and picks up until 6 p.m. Our address for the 911 dispatcher is 14 Alder Street. The neighbors at number 16 are home most evenings and have a key.

## Bedtime

Lily's bath is at 7, books, lights out by 7:45 with the hall light on. Max can read until 8:30. No screens after 7:30.

## Snacks and meals

Dinner is in the fridge, ready to warm. Snacks are in the bottom drawer. No nuts for either child, and nothing from the shelf marked with the red tape in the pantry.

## Max's bee allergy

Max is severely allergic to bee and wasp stings. His two epinephrine auto-injectors are in the red bag on the hook by the front door, and the bag goes wherever he goes outside. If he is stung: take the auto-injector out of the red bag, pull off the safety cap, press the tip into the outside of his thigh and hold it for 3 seconds. Then call 911 right away, even if he seems fine, and then call Mom and Dad. Do not wait to see if it gets worse, and do not give him a drink or food.

## Lily's asthma

Lily's inhaler and spacer are in the kitchen drawer next to the fridge. If she coughs or wheezes, give 2 puffs with the spacer and sit her quietly. If she is still struggling after 20 minutes, call 911.

## House rules

No friends over. Doors locked after dark. Do not open the door to anyone you do not know.
